papers.title: DHX15 as a novel immune-related prognostic biomarker in breast cancer: An integrated bioinformatics analysis with in vitro functional validation.
papers.abstract: Breast cancer (BC) is a disease that occurs relatively frequently, and its prognosis and treatment outcomes are not optimal at present. Identifying novel BC biomarkers and therapeutic targets is key. DEAH-box helicase 15 (DHX15) is an RNA helicase that exhibits enhanced activity and is closely associated with tumorigenic potential. Alternative splicing is widely dysregulated in BC. However, the biological function of DHX15 in BC, in addition to its underlying molecular mechanisms, remain unclear. DHX15, a key RNA helicase involved in splicing regulation, was therefore selected to explore wheth
papers.summary: This study identifies DHX15 as a potential immune-related prognostic biomarker in breast cancer through integrated bioinformatics analysis and in vitro functional validation. The findings suggest that DHX15 expression is associated with patient prognosis and immune infiltration, highlighting its potential as a therapeutic target.

papers.title: Proteomic profiling of isolated mouse endometrial epithelial cells reveals coordinated redox and endoplasmic reticulum stress-associated pathways during uterine receptivity.
papers.abstract: Uterine receptivity is critical for successful embryo implantation, yet epithelial-specific proteomic changes during this transition remain incompletely characterized. This study aimed to profile changes in protein expression in isolated mouse endometrial epithelial cells between the pre-receptive (Day 1) and receptive (Day 4) phases of pregnancy to identify key pathways associated with uterine receptivity.
papers.summary: This study profiles protein expression changes in mouse endometrial epithelial cells between pre-receptive and receptive phases of pregnancy, identifying coordinated redox and endoplasmic reticulum stress-associated pathways that may be important for uterine receptivity and embryo implantation.

papers.title: Integrative analysis of HMGB3 in esophageal carcinoma: expression profile, prognostic significance, and immune microenvironment associations.
papers.abstract: Esophageal carcinoma (ESCA) remains highly lethal and lacks robust biomarkers for early detection and risk stratification. High mobility group box 3 (HMGB3) has been implicated as an oncogene in several cancers, but its role in ESCA has not been fully defined. To address these clinical and biological gaps, this study systematically characterized the expression profile, diagnostic and prognostic value, biological functions, and immune-related features of HMGB3 in ESCA through integrative bioinformatics analyses and in vitro validation.
papers.summary: This study systematically characterized HMGB3 in esophageal carcinoma using integrative bioinformatics and in vitro experiments, finding that HMGB3 is overexpressed in tumors, correlates with poor prognosis, and is associated with immune infiltration. The findings suggest HMGB3 could serve as a prognostic biomarker and potential therapeutic target in ESCA.

papers.title: Beyond omics: From descriptive profiling to causal and scalable design of fermentation microbiomes.
papers.abstract: Fermentation microbiomes play essential roles in food production, feed preservation, waste valorization, and diverse sustainable industrial processes. Although multi-omics and systems biology have substantially advanced our understanding of their assembly, interactions, and functional dynamics, industrial translation remains constrained by fragmented datasets, limited causal validation, and transport constraints during scale-up. Large language models act as upper-level knowledge and workflow orchestrators, accelerating data integration, hybrid AI-mechanistic modeling, hypothesis generation, an
papers.summary: This review discusses how multi-omics and systems biology have advanced our understanding of fermentation microbiomes but notes that industrial translation is limited by fragmented data and scale-up challenges. It proposes that large language models can serve as knowledge orchestrators to accelerate data integration, hybrid AI-mechanistic modeling, and hypothesis generation, enabling a shift from descriptive profiling to causal and scalable design of fermentation microbiomes.

papers.title: Determinants influencing triage system at tertiary care centre as perceived by triage nurse: a qualitative study.
papers.abstract: The objective of this study is to explore the lived experiences of triage nurses.
papers.summary: This qualitative study explores the lived experiences of triage nurses at a tertiary care center to identify factors that influence the triage system. The findings highlight key determinants such as workload, communication challenges, and resource limitations, which impact triage accuracy and efficiency.

papers.title: Candidate metabolites in sepsis-associated encephalopathy: Network analysis and in vitro validation of glycitein.
papers.abstract: Sepsis-associated encephalopathy (SAE) is a severe neurological complication of sepsis. Cerebrovascular endothelial injury serves as a key contributor to its pathogenesis, and metabolite-mediated inflammatory regulation may be involved in this process. However, the specific candidate metabolites and their underlying pathways remain poorly characterized. This study aimed to identify candidate metabolites related to SAE through network pharmacology and to provide preliminary in vitro validation.
papers.summary: This study uses network pharmacology to identify candidate metabolites involved in sepsis-associated encephalopathy (SAE), focusing on cerebrovascular endothelial injury and inflammatory regulation. The authors highlight glycitein as a potential protective metabolite and provide preliminary in vitro validation of its effects.

papers.title: Spatial omics illuminates tumor heterogeneity.
papers.abstract: Intratumoral heterogeneity (ITH) is the coexistence of diverse cancer cell states, genotypes, and microenvironmental niches within a single tumor and is a major driver of therapeutic resistance and disease progression. While the clinical implications of ITH are well appreciated, conventional methods and models have been limited in resolving the spatial and functional complexity underlying ITH. Recent advances in single-cell and spatial omics, high-plex imaging, and in vivo CRISPR perturbation and lineage tracing now enable unprecedented, mechanistic dissection of tumor ecosystems. These techno
papers.summary: This review discusses how recent advances in single-cell and spatial omics, high-plex imaging, and in vivo CRISPR perturbation and lineage tracing are enabling unprecedented mechanistic dissection of intratumoral heterogeneity (ITH). It highlights how these technologies can resolve the spatial and functional complexity of tumor ecosystems, which is critical for understanding therapeutic resistance and disease progression.

papers.title: Advancing cross-domain integration and semantic technologies: proceedings of the 19th international symposium on integrative bioinformatics.
papers.abstract: This special issue of the Journal of Integrative Bioinformatics presents proceedings from the 19th International Symposium on Integrative Bioinformatics, which was held 10-12 September 2025. The featured contributions address critical bottlenecks in life science data management, specifically focusing on the practical implementation of FAIR (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, and Reusable) principles as an essential prerequisite for data integration and data interoperability. Comprising nine peer-reviewed articles, the issue highlights methodological advancements in cross-omics integration, s
papers.summary: This special issue presents proceedings from the 19th International Symposium on Integrative Bioinformatics, highlighting methodological advances in cross-omics data integration and the practical implementation of FAIR principles to address bottlenecks in life science data management. The nine peer-reviewed articles focus on improving data interoperability and integration across diverse biological datasets.

papers.title: A haplotype-resolved, chromosome-scale genome assembly and annotation for Carya glabra (pignut hickory; Juglandaceae).
papers.abstract: Carya glabra (2n = 4x = 64), also known as pignut hickory, is a widely distributed species in the walnut family (Juglandaceae). Native to the central and eastern United States and southeastern Canada, C. glabra plays an important ecological role as a common upland forest species; it is closely related to several economically valuable nut trees, including Carya illinoinensis (pecan). A deeper understanding of the genetics of C. glabra is essential for studying its evolutionary history and biology, with potential implications for agricultural improvement of pecan. Here, we present the first nucl
papers.summary: This study presents the first haplotype-resolved, chromosome-scale genome assembly and annotation for Carya glabra (pignut hickory), a tetraploid species in the walnut family. The new genomic resource will facilitate studies of evolutionary history and biology in hickories, with potential applications for improving related crops like pecan.

papers.title: Association of IL-8 and IL-18 Expression With Histone-Associated NETosis in Aqueous-Deficient and Evaporative Dry Eye Disease.
papers.abstract: Dry eye disease (DED) is a chronic inflammatory disorder of the ocular surface; however, upstream immune mechanisms contributing to DED are complex and unclear. This study aimed to identify differentially expressed tear proteins in patients with DED and elucidate the underlying disease mechanism.
papers.summary: This study identifies differentially expressed tear proteins in patients with dry eye disease (DED), specifically linking elevated IL-8 and IL-18 expression to histone-associated NETosis (a form of neutrophil cell death) in both aqueous-deficient and evaporative DED subtypes. The findings suggest that NETosis and these inflammatory cytokines may be key upstream immune mechanisms driving ocular surface inflammation in DED.

papers.title: PathMED: an R toolkit for single-sample molecular scoring and machine learning with omics data.
papers.abstract: Molecular scoring is a popular approach for studying pathway-level functional alterations with omics data. Using molecular scores for tasks such as single-sample molecular characterisation, phenotype prediction or disease stratification has several advantages compared to using omics data directly. Molecular scores provide biological interpretability and are more generalisable across datasets, facilitating data integration and machine learning applications. However, numerous scoring methods are available through different software packages, and currently there is a lack of tools to easily use t
papers.summary: PathMED is a new R toolkit that simplifies single-sample molecular scoring and machine learning with omics data, addressing the lack of integrated tools for this purpose. It provides a unified interface for multiple scoring methods and downstream ML tasks, enhancing interpretability and cross-dataset generalizability.

papers.title: Integrating short-read and long-read single-cell transcriptomics of pig pituitary reveals mechanisms of high-altitude hypoxia adaptation.
papers.abstract: Acting as the central endocrine hub, the pituitary gland is closely related to the mechanism of adaptation to high-altitude hypoxia. Here, by integratively combining long-read (Oxford Nanopore) and short-read (Illumina) single-cell sequencing approaches, we profiled pituitaries from Diqing Tibetan pigs, inhabiting high-altitude environments (3,200 m) and Diannan small-ear pigs from low-altitude regions (500 m), thereby generating a full-length single-cell atlas, which in turn enabled the identification of molecular mechanisms potentially underlying adaptation to high-altitude hypoxia stress. S
papers.summary: This study integrates long-read and short-read single-cell transcriptomics to profile pituitary glands from high-altitude (Tibetan) and low-altitude (Diannan small-ear) pigs, generating a full-length single-cell atlas. The analysis identifies molecular mechanisms, including cell-type-specific gene expression and isoform usage, that may underlie adaptation to high-altitude hypoxia stress.

papers.title: IP-LC-MS/MS-Based Identification of Candidate TPL2 (MAP3K8)-Associated Proteins in Porcine PK-15 Cells.
papers.abstract: Tumor progression locus 2 (TPL2, also known as MAP-3K8/COT) is a kinase that regulates MAPK and NF-κB signaling and contributes to antiviral immunity. While mammalian TPL2 has been widely studied, the TPL2-associated protein profile in swine cells remains largely unexplored. In this study, we generated an IP-LC-MS/MS-based candidate dataset of TPL2-associated proteins in porcine kidney epithelial (PK-15) cells. FLAG-tagged TPL2 was overexpressed in PK-15 cells and enriched by immunoprecipitation, followed by liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) analysis. After subtraction
papers.summary: This study generated the first candidate interactome of TPL2 (MAP3K8) in porcine PK-15 cells using immunoprecipitation followed by LC-MS/MS, identifying potential TPL2-associated proteins that may regulate MAPK/NF-κB signaling and antiviral immunity. The dataset provides a foundation for future functional studies of TPL2 in swine and comparative analysis across species.

papers.title: Nigericin-Triggered Phosphodynamics in Inflammasome Formation and Pyroptosis.
papers.abstract: Innate immune signaling relies heavily on phosphorylation cascades to mount effective immune responses. Although traditional innate immune signaling cascades following TLR4 stimulation have been investigated through a temporally quantitative phosphoproteomic lens, far fewer studies have applied these methods to distinct signaling following the inflammasome trigger leading to IL-1β release. Here, we conducted time-resolved phosphoproteomic profiling to investigate kinase signaling downstream of the inflammasome trigger nigericin. We found that nigericin induces rapid and potent alterations in t
papers.summary: This study uses time-resolved phosphoproteomics to map kinase signaling downstream of the inflammasome trigger nigericin, revealing rapid and potent phosphorylation changes that drive inflammasome formation and pyroptosis. It provides a new resource for understanding innate immune signaling beyond TLR4 pathways.

papers.title: Transcriptomic and epigenomic insights into ovarian cancer: a bioinformatics perspective - a narrative review.
papers.abstract: Ovarian cancer is a highly heterogeneous malignancy with complex molecular underpinnings that extend beyond genomic mutations to encompass transcriptomic and epigenomic alterations. Advances in next-generation sequencing and bioinformatics have enabled comprehensive profiling of gene expression patterns, non-coding RNAs, DNA methylation, histone modifications, and chromatin accessibility, offering novel insights into ovarian tumor biology. Transcriptomic analyses reveal dysregulated coding and non-coding RNA networks, while epigenomic studies uncover epigenetic modifications that regulate gene
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes recent bioinformatics-driven transcriptomic and epigenomic studies of ovarian cancer, highlighting how gene expression and epigenetic alterations contribute to tumor heterogeneity and biology. It emphasizes the utility of next-generation sequencing and computational approaches for uncovering novel biomarkers and therapeutic targets.

papers.title: Targeting Spatiotemporal Heterogeneity of oncomiRNAs: A New Frontier in Cancer Therapy.
papers.abstract: miRNAs are short RNA transcripts that modulate gene expression after transcription and have emerged as pivotal regulators of cancer biology. A subset, termed oncomiRNAs, functions as oncogenes or tumor suppressors, influencing key cellular events such as cell growth, programmed cell death, neovascularization, tissue invasion, and metastatic spread. Dysregulation of these miRNAs drives tumor initiation and progression, underscoring their role in cancer evolution. Traditionally, studies have relied on bulk tissue analyses, overlooking the profound spatiotemporal heterogeneity of oncomiRNA expres
papers.summary: This review discusses the emerging importance of oncomiRNAs—miRNAs that act as oncogenes or tumor suppressors—in cancer biology, highlighting how their dysregulation drives tumor initiation and progression. It emphasizes that traditional bulk tissue analyses overlook the spatiotemporal heterogeneity of oncomiRNA expression, and proposes that targeting this heterogeneity represents a new frontier in cancer therapy.

papers.title: Integrated Network Analysis Suggests an miR-21/MMP/VEGF-Associated Regulatory Axis in Gastric Cancer.
papers.abstract: Gastric cancer (GC) pathogenesis involves complex molecular interactions that remain incompletely understood at a biological systems level. While microRNA-21 (miR-21), matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs), and vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) have been individually implicated in GC, their integrated role as a coordinated regulatory network remains uncharacterized. And we aim to reveal novel biology systems level insights into the miR-21/MMP/VEGF regulatory axis.
papers.summary: This study uses integrated network analysis to characterize a coordinated regulatory axis involving miR-21, matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs), and vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) in gastric cancer, providing systems-level insights into their combined role in tumor progression. The findings suggest that these molecules function as an interconnected network, potentially offering new targets for therapy or biomarkers.

papers.title: Circulating multi-omic signature of disease severity and cholangiocarcinoma in primary sclerosing cholangitis.
papers.abstract: Primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) is a chronic cholestatic liver disease often associated with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) that can progress to cirrhosis or cholangiocarcinoma (CCA), both carrying a poor prognosis. The mechanisms driving disease progression remain poorly understood. We aimed to identify circulating multi-omic signatures linked to PSC severity (alkaline phosphatase, bilirubin, fibrosis), IBD, and CCA to elucidate underlying biology and discover potential biomarkers for risk stratification and disease monitoring.
papers.summary: This study identifies circulating multi-omic signatures associated with disease severity and cholangiocarcinoma in primary sclerosing cholangitis, potentially revealing underlying biological mechanisms and offering biomarkers for risk stratification and monitoring.

papers.title: From parasite biology to predictive metabolic models.
papers.abstract: Protist parasites cause devastating diseases worldwide, yet their complex metabolism remains poorly understood. Genome-scale metabolic models (GEMs) have emerged as powerful tools to systematically represent and simulate parasite metabolism, enabling the prediction of gene essentiality, metabolic vulnerabilities, and host-parasite interactions. This review examines the current landscape of GEMs for protist pathogens, focusing on the key modeling decisions (objective functions, constraints, and compartmentalization) that govern model behavior and predictive scope. We discuss how these choices s
papers.summary: This review discusses the use of genome-scale metabolic models (GEMs) to study the metabolism of protist parasites, highlighting how modeling decisions like objective functions and constraints affect predictions of gene essentiality and host-parasite interactions. It provides an overview of current GEMs for these pathogens and their potential for identifying metabolic vulnerabilities.

papers.title: The Data Science of Health in Space.
papers.abstract: Spaceflight exposes humans to unique stressors that remodel biology. Space health is emerging as a data science discipline grounded in multiomic atlases, harmonized biobanks, and open, findable, accessible, interoperable, and reusable (FAIR)-aligned infrastructures. We review this ecosystem, including the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA)'s GeneLab; the Open Science Data Repository, European Space Agency, and Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA) platforms; the Space Omics and Medical Atlas; and mission-specific repositories, and how it is used to integrate heterogeneous
papers.journal: Annual review of biomedical data science
papers.summary: This review describes the emerging field of space health as a data science discipline, highlighting the role of multiomic atlases, harmonized biobanks, and FAIR-aligned data infrastructures such as NASA's GeneLab and the Space Omics and Medical Atlas. It discusses how these resources enable the integration of heterogeneous data to understand how spaceflight stressors remodel human biology.

papers.title: Implementation of a computational medical assemblage heuristic to improve rational design of phytomedicines for safety, efficacy and regulatory approval.
papers.abstract: Phytomedicines are key to global healthcare and underutilized in Western medical systems. The inherent complexity of multi-species polypharmaceutical formulations presents barriers (standardization, reproducibility and regulatory approval) that can relegate potentially safe, effective and lower cost medication to nutraceutical settings in countries such as the US. The identification of Minimal Essential Effective Formulations (MEEFs) is a strategy to rationally simplify phytomedicines while preserving efficacy, but it requires computational innovation to de-risk and prioritize compounds due to
papers.summary: This paper proposes a computational heuristic to rationally design phytomedicines by identifying Minimal Essential Effective Formulations (MEEFs), aiming to simplify complex multi-species formulations while preserving efficacy and improving safety, standardization, and regulatory approval. The approach addresses key barriers to integrating phytomedicines into Western healthcare systems.

papers.title: Characterization of long non-coding RNAs during compatible and incompatible pollination in Arabidopsis thaliana.
papers.abstract: Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) have emerged as critical players in plant development and stress responses, yet their involvement in pollination responses is largely unknown. To address this gap, we identified and characterized lncRNAs and their predicted cis-acting, trans-acting, and miRNA-mediated possible regulatory interactions during both compatible and incompatible pollination in Arabidopsis thaliana. Leveraging publicly available datasets, we analyzed expression profiles at 10 and 60 minutes post-pollination. We identified 1,073 novel and 3,422 annotated lncRNA loci, with 1,002 novel and
papers.summary: This study characterizes long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) and their potential regulatory interactions during compatible and incompatible pollination in Arabidopsis thaliana, identifying thousands of novel and annotated lncRNA loci with dynamic expression changes. The findings provide a foundation for understanding how lncRNAs may contribute to pollination responses, though functional validation is still needed.

papers.title: De novo whole transcriptome sequencing reveals differentially expressed messenger RNA and MicroRNA in hepatopancreas of Pandalus hypsinotus.
papers.abstract: Pandalus hypsinotus (P. hypsinotus), also known as coonstripe shrimp, has high economic value and is widely distributed in Alaska, the Bering Sea and the East Sea of Korea. However, owing to the low catch rates and patchy spatial distribution, transcriptome-based studies on this species remain limited. Transcriptome analyses using PacBio Iso-Seq and Illumina RNA sequencing techniques were performed to establish a de novo unigene set of P. hypsinotus and identify differentially expressed genes (DEGs) in the hepatopancreas compared to the tail muscle. A search of all the unigenes against Gene On
papers.summary: This study generated a de novo transcriptome for the coonstripe shrimp (Pandalus hypsinotus) using PacBio and Illumina sequencing, identifying differentially expressed mRNAs and microRNAs in the hepatopancreas compared to tail muscle. The findings provide a valuable genetic resource for this economically important but understudied species, and reveal potential molecular pathways involved in hepatopancreas-specific functions.

papers.title: Leveraging expression quantitative trait loci information in single-cell resolution to identify cell-specific genes for Basal cell carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Basal cell carcinoma (BCC), the most common skin cancer, is driven by UV-induced DNA damage and shaped by immune surveillance. Although GWAS has identified over 140 risk loci, their cell-type-specific effects remain obscured by tissue-level averaging.
papers.summary: This study integrates expression quantitative trait loci (eQTL) data with single-cell RNA sequencing to identify cell-type-specific genes associated with basal cell carcinoma (BCC) risk, moving beyond tissue-level averages to reveal immune and stromal cell contributions. The approach highlights how leveraging single-cell resolution can uncover the cellular context of GWAS hits, potentially guiding more targeted therapeutic strategies for BCC.
